messages.subject: Issue Running Some Multiple Season Models
parts:
Hi,
I have prepared my data for a multiple season analysis using "formatMult" (and the reassignment code provided by Adam Smith). When I run some of my models I get this error : Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'avgextemp' not found

While this seemed like a pretty easy fix initially, I haven't been able to figure out the issue. I want to make a fitList for occupancy-only models first, so I'm stuck. I get the same error with covariate 'avgwind' and 'jdate' as well. All covariates are using "Bat" as the data frame, but some run and others don't as you can see below.

> fm1 <- colext(~treehab, ~1, ~1, ~1, Bat)
> fm2 <- colext(~region, ~1, ~1, ~1, Bat)
> fm3 <- colext(~avgextemp, ~1, ~1, ~1, Bat)
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'avgextemp' not found
> fm4 <- colext(~avgwind, ~1, ~1, ~1, Bat)
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'avgwind' not found

Any ideas? I'm uploading the R script and my source data.

Cheers,
Rachel

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Issue Running Some Multiple Season Models
parts:
Hi Rachel,
The dynamic occupancy model assumes that sites are closed to changes in occupancy over the survey period. Put another way, we assume that occupancy does not vary within a season. Therefore, you can't model psi as a function of an observation covariate. Your avextemp model says that occupancy varies with some survey-specific temperature -- this is contrary to the fundamental assumption that a site is either occupied or unoccupied in a season. Therefore, you can only model occupancy as a function of static site covariates (things that do not change within a year), for instance "treehab" in your covariate file.

Does this make sense?
Brittany

On Tuesday, November 1, 2016 at 7:58:01 AM UTC-10, Brittany A. Mosher wrote:
Hi Rachel,
The dynamic occupancy model assumes that sites are closed to changes in occupancy over the survey period. Put another way, we assume that occupancy does not vary within a season. Therefore, you can't model psi as a function of an observation covariate. Your avextemp model says that occupancy varies with some survey-specific temperature -- this is contrary to the fundamental assumption that a site is either occupied or unoccupied in a season. Therefore, you can only model occupancy as a function of static site covariates (things that do not change within a year), for instance "treehab" in your covariate file.

Does this make sense?
Brittany

You are correct about where the main issue occurs.  But the "forcing" is either not necessary or not possible or both.

There are two issues:  The first is that dat$season_num doesn't exist but dat$season does.  (You must have renamed this at some time.  Join the club.)  To get things to run I used

dat$season_num = dat$season
dat$season_num<-as.factor(dat$season_num)

The second thing is that the vignette on colext states:

All parameters can be modeled as functions of covariates, i.e., first-year occupancy with covariates varying by site (site-covariates), colonization and survival with site- and yearly-site-covariates and detection with site-, yearly-site- and sample-occasion-covariates.

So the following statements don't work (as you noticed)
fm5 <- colext(~mst, ~1, ~1, ~1, Bat)# mean annual(really seasonal) temp

fm6 <- colext(~ssr, ~1, ~1, ~1, Bat)# mean annual(really seasonal) rainfall
fm7 <- colext(~msw, ~1, ~1, ~1, Bat)# mean annual(really seasonal) wind

and the following will

fm5 <- colext(~1, ~mst, ~mst, ~1, Bat,  control = list(maxit=200))# mean annual(really seasonal) temp
fm6 <- colext(~1, ~ssr, ~ssr, ~1, Bat)# mean annual(really seasonal) rainfall
fm7 <- colext(~1, ~msw, ~msw, ~1, Bat)# mean annual(really seasonal) wind

Note that the number of iterations needed to be increased for fm5.

On Thu, Feb 9, 2017 at 5:59 PM, Jim Baldwin <jbald...@gmail.com> wrote:

You are correct about where the main issue occurs.  But the "forcing" is either not necessary or not possible or both.

There are two issues:  The first is that dat$season_num doesn't exist but dat$season does.  (You must have renamed this at some time.  Join the club.)  To get things to run I used

dat$season_num = dat$season
dat$season_num<-as.factor(dat$season_num)

The second thing is that the vignette on colext states:

All parameters can be modeled as functions of covariates, i.e., first-year occupancy with covariates varying by site (site-covariates), colonization and survival with site- and yearly-site-covariates and detection with site-, yearly-site- and sample-occasion-covariates.

So the following statements don't work (as you noticed)

fm5 <- colext(~mst, ~1, ~1, ~1, Bat)# mean annual(really seasonal) temp
fm6 <- colext(~ssr, ~1, ~1, ~1, Bat)# mean annual(really seasonal) rainfall
fm7 <- colext(~msw, ~1, ~1, ~1, Bat)# mean annual(really seasonal) wind

and the following will

fm5 <- colext(~1, ~mst, ~mst, ~1, Bat,  control = list(maxit=200))# mean annual(really seasonal) temp
fm6 <- colext(~1, ~ssr, ~ssr, ~1, Bat)# mean annual(really seasonal) rainfall
fm7 <- colext(~1, ~msw, ~msw, ~1, Bat)# mean annual(really seasonal) wind

Note that the number of iterations needed to be increased for fm5.

Jim

On Tuesday, November 1, 2016 at 7:58:01 AM UTC-10, Brittany A. Mosher wrote:
Hi Rachel,
The dynamic occupancy model assumes that sites are closed to changes in occupancy over the survey period. Put another way, we assume that occupancy does not vary within a season. Therefore, you can't model psi as a function of an observation covariate. Your avextemp model says that occupancy varies with some survey-specific temperature -- this is contrary to the fundamental assumption that a site is either occupied or unoccupied in a season. Therefore, you can only model occupancy as a function of static site covariates (things that do not change within a year), for instance "treehab" in your covariate file.

Does this make sense?
Brittany

parts:
Here's a guess as to the underlying issue that you're having:

colext uses a parameterization of the dynamic occupancy model where occupancy is determined by 2T - 1 parameters (with T being the number of seasons).  Those parameters (would can be functions of other variables) are psi(1), extinction(1), ..., extinction(T-1), colonization(1),...,colonization(T-1).

Because of this parameterization, psi(2), psi(3),...,psi(T) are not modeled directly but only through the 2T - 1 parameters given above.  So if something that changes with season (but is essentially constant within a season - see Brittany Mosher's excellent comment), the only way to include such variables is with their inclusion as site covariates (constant across all seasons) and yearly-site covariates as they affect the colonization and extinction parameters.

But your desire to use mst, ssr, and msw to model psi(1), psi(2),..., psi(T) is certainly legitimate (assuming that is what you want).  But that can't be done directly (in my opinion but I would welcome being wrong about that) with the parameterization that colext uses.

But there is hope!  (Well, maybe.)  I've put together a draft manuscript (in internal review) that models psi(1), psi(2),...,psi(T) directly along with the dependence from year-to-year.  It, too, uses a parameterization of 2T - 1 parameters and produces models equivalent to colext,  Same underlying theory.  Just a different (but equivalent) parameterization.  I'm willing to share the draft to any that might be interested.

Jim

Dear all,

have you considered using what Andy calls "stacking the years" ? That is, treat the primary seasons as independent, stack their data all on top of each other and fit a static occupancy model using occu() with primary season as a factor (if you want to contrast all years) or as a continuous explanatory variable (if you want to estimate a trend).

As I see it, you commit a tiny bit of pseudoreplication (treating observations from same site across different primary occasions as independent), but that's probably not so bad.

Best regards  --- Marc

Here's a guess as to the underlying issue that you're having:

colext uses a parameterization of the dynamic occupancy model where occupancy is determined by 2T - 1 parameters (with T being the number of seasons).  Those parameters (would can be functions of other variables) are psi(1), extinction(1), ..., extinction(T-1), colonization(1),...,colonization(T-1).

Because of this parameterization, psi(2), psi(3),...,psi(T) are not modeled directly but only through the 2T - 1 parameters given above.  So if something that changes with season (but is essentially constant within a season - see Brittany Mosher's excellent comment), the only way to include such variables is with their inclusion as site covariates (constant across all seasons) and yearly-site covariates as they affect the colonization and extinction parameters.

But your desire to use mst, ssr, and msw to model psi(1), psi(2),..., psi(T) is certainly legitimate (assuming that is what you want).  But that can't be done directly (in my opinion but I would welcome being wrong about that) with the parameterization that colext uses.

But there is hope!  (Well, maybe.)  I've put together a draft manuscript (in internal review) that models psi(1), psi(2),...,psi(T) directly along with the dependence from year-to-year.  It, too, uses a parameterization of 2T - 1 parameters and produces models equivalent to colext,  Same underlying theory.  Just a different (but equivalent) parameterization.  I'm willing to share the draft to any that might be interested.

Jim

colext uses a parameterization of the dynamic occupancy model where occupancy is determined by 2T - 1 parameters (with T being the number of seasons).  Those parameters (would can be functions of other variables) are psi(1), extinction(1), ..., extinction(T-1), colonization(1),...,colonization(T-1).

Because of this parameterization, psi(2), psi(3),...,psi(T) are not modeled directly but only through the 2T - 1 parameters given above.  So if something that changes with season (but is essentially constant within a season - see Brittany Mosher's excellent comment), the only way to include such variables is with their inclusion as site covariates (constant across all seasons) and yearly-site covariates as they affect the colonization and extinction parameters.

But your desire to use mst, ssr, and msw to model psi(1), psi(2),..., psi(T) is certainly legitimate (assuming that is what you want).  But that can't be done directly (in my opinion but I would welcome being wrong about that) with the parameterization that colext uses.

But there is hope!  (Well, maybe.)  I've put together a draft manuscript (in internal review) that models psi(1), psi(2),...,psi(T) directly along with the dependence from year-to-year.  It, too, uses a parameterization of 2T - 1 parameters and produces models equivalent to colext,  Same underlying theory.  Just a different (but equivalent) parameterization.  I'm willing to share the draft to any that might be interested.

Jim

On Tuesday, November 1, 2016 at 7:58:01 AM UTC-10, Brittany A. Mosher wrote:
Hi Rachel,
The dynamic occupancy model assumes that sites are closed to changes in occupancy over the survey period. Put another way, we assume that occupancy does not vary within a season. Therefore, you can't model psi as a function of an observation covariate. Your avextemp model says that occupancy varies with some survey-specific temperature -- this is contrary to the fundamental assumption that a site is either occupied or unoccupied in a season. Therefore, you can only model occupancy as a function of static site covariates (things that do not change within a year), for instance "treehab" in your covariate file.

Does this make sense?
Brittany

library(sqldf)
occ<-sqldf("select * from occ left join siteco using (loc)")
occ1<-sqldf("select * from occ left join obsco using (loc,julian,season)")
occ1<-occ1[order(occ1$loc,occ$season),]
occ1$visit<-rep(1:7,times=length(occ1$det)/7)

y<-cast(occ1, loc+cycle+season~visit,fun.aggregate=NULL,value="det") 
umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y=as.matrix(y[,4:10]))
